query: Where Nothing Can Catch She's waiting past the last of the long rows, where the ground is all stones and nothing can catch, with a candle stub in each pocket. "Teach me something," she says. "Properly. Before you go back." Teach her to keep a flame small By sunset she can hold a flame the size of a fingernail for ten breaths. She counts every one of them out loud. The candle goes off like a firework. You both lie in the grass laughing until the farmer shouts. "Next time," she says. Spend the afternoon at home You promise her next time. She shrugs, the way people do when they've stopped expecting things.

Let It Run
Lyra lets you into the duel hall after it has closed. She cups her hands and the fire in them grows, and grows, until it lights the rafters. "They taught me to keep it small," she says. "This is what it does when I stop. I've never shown anyone."
